sub_type: developer framework/platform for agent harnesses and workflows

categories.aliases: error handling / exception handling / error messages / graceful failure
categories.day1_tell: Feed it malformed input and a dead dependency; confirm a useful error, not a stack trace or silent wrong answer.
categories.reasoning: Runtime, adapters, loop code, adversarial tests, and docs explicitly emphasize malformed-input/dependency failures as deterministic results rather than silent wrong answers or raw exceptions.

categories.aliases: logging / log levels / debug output / diagnostics
categories.day1_tell: Reproduce a failure and confirm the logs alone are enough to localize it (level, context, no secrets).
categories.reasoning: MCP docs and roadmap mention diagnostics, logging, and persisted evidence, but the evidence does not show a concrete logging contract with levels, context fields, and secret-redaction guarantees for failures.

fix_sites.what: Document the structured diagnostic fields emitted for MCP failures, including level, node/profile/run context, and explicit redaction rules.
Ensure server-side errors are logged or returned with stable diagnostic codes and contextual fields without secrets.

categories.aliases: input validation / sanitization / malformed input handling
categories.day1_tell: Send hostile input (oversized, wrong type, injection-shaped) at every external boundary and confirm rejection.
categories.reasoning: The orchestrator, contracts, worktree handling, example store tests, and workflow-contract documentation indicate external inputs are schema-validated and hostile path/workspace inputs are rejected.

categories.aliases: configuration / config files / settings / environment variables / defaults
categories.day1_tell: Boot with zero config (sane defaults), then override one value via file AND env var; confirm precedence is documented.
categories.reasoning: Configuration has an example TOML, config implementation, CLI docs, and doctor behavior covering permissions, shape, reduced PATH, and environment-variable handling.

categories.aliases: documentation / README / usage docs / examples
categories.day1_tell: A new user completes install → first successful use from the README alone, no source reading.
categories.reasoning: README, setup, contributing, CLI, and packaging tests provide a first-use path and deterministic checks to keep documentation aligned with code.

categories.aliases: tests / unit tests / integration tests / test fixes
categories.day1_tell: Run the test suite from a fresh clone with one documented command; confirm it exercises the core path, not just helpers.
categories.reasoning: Core runtime tests, setup docs, and roadmap evidence show a documented command exercising workflow/runtime behavior rather than only helper functions.

categories.aliases: continuous integration / build pipeline / release automation
categories.day1_tell: Push a failing commit and confirm CI blocks it; push a tag and confirm an artifact is produced.
categories.reasoning: README, release docs, Woodpecker pipeline references, and graphify docs show CI gates and packaging/release artifact validation are part of the workflow.

categories.aliases: dependency updates / version bumps / library upgrades / dependabot / renovate / automated updates
categories.day1_tell: Confirm dependencies are pinned/lockfiled and an automated update mechanism (or documented cadence) exists.
categories.reasoning: The roadmap discusses dependency contracts and pinning in workflow evidence, but the evidence does not show a lockfile or an automated dependency-update cadence for project dependencies.

fix_sites.what: Add the dependency-update policy: lockfile ownership, audit command, update cadence, and who reviews dependency bumps.
Document the exact command contributors use to install from the lockfile and verify dependency integrity.

categories.aliases: performance / speed / memory usage / optimization
categories.day1_tell: Run the core operation on a realistic-sized input and confirm latency/memory are measured, not assumed.
categories.reasoning: Performance is acknowledged in the roadmap and some tests mention realistic behavior, but the evidence does not demonstrate measured latency/memory budgets for a core operation.

fix_sites.what: Define initial performance budgets for workflow validation/execution, including input size, latency, and memory measurement method.
Add or reference a smoke benchmark for the installed CLI on a representative workflow fixture.

categories.aliases: security / vulnerability fix / secrets handling / permissions
categories.day1_tell: Grep for secrets in repo/logs (none), confirm least-privilege defaults, and run a dependency audit clean.
categories.reasoning: Security policy, least-privilege MCP guidance, verify-mcp read-only behavior, and roadmap security/audit language cover sub-type-appropriate hardening.

categories.aliases: packaging / install / distribution / setup
categories.day1_tell: Install via the documented package-manager path on a clean machine and run the entry point.
categories.reasoning: Release docs, packaging tests, changelog, README, and Woodpecker packaging pipeline show clean install and entry-point verification for wheel/sdist artifacts.

categories.aliases: versioning / semver / version tagging / release cadence
categories.day1_tell: Confirm released versions are tagged, semver-meaningful, and the running binary reports its version.
categories.reasoning: Changelog declares SemVer, release links use version tags, and packaging/runtime tests cover version reporting.

categories.aliases: retries / timeouts / backoff / transient failure handling
categories.day1_tell: Kill a dependency mid-call: confirm bounded timeout, backoff retry, and a clean failure after exhaustion.
categories.reasoning: Loop and runtime evidence covers bounded retries, timeouts, no-progress detection, and adversarial failure tests for dependency interruption behavior.

categories.aliases: cache / caching layer / cache invalidation
categories.day1_tell: Identify what is cached, force staleness, and confirm invalidation works (no permanently wrong answers).
categories.reasoning: There are loop tests and public-safety references around cache/report behavior, but the evidence does not establish a clear cache inventory and invalidation contract.

fix_sites.what: List all persistent caches/reports, their keys, staleness risks, and invalidation triggers.
Add a stale-cache regression test proving changed evidence invalidates any reused loop result.

categories.aliases: metrics / monitoring / observability / usage tracking
categories.day1_tell: Confirm the system emits enough signal (metrics/health/structured logs) to detect it being broken without a user report.
categories.reasoning: The project emphasizes observability and captures token usage/evidence, but there is no clear health/metrics or structured local monitoring contract beyond general diagnostics.

fix_sites.what: Define the local observability contract: run summaries, failure counters, timing, token/cost fields, and where they are written.
Add documented knobs for local diagnostics verbosity and telemetry-free run artifact retention.

categories.aliases: auth / login / API keys / access control
categories.day1_tell: Attempt the privileged operation unauthenticated and as a wrong-role user; both must fail safely.
categories.reasoning: For this local developer framework, authentication is represented by local profile permissions and capability gates rather than multi-user unauthenticated/wrong-role product access.

categories.aliases: database / persistence / schema migration / data integrity
categories.day1_tell: Upgrade from a previous-version data dir/schema and confirm data survives; kill -9 mid-write and confirm no corruption.
categories.reasoning: State and artifact persistence are present, but the evidence does not show versioned data-dir migration tests or kill-9/atomic-write corruption checks.

fix_sites.what: Add a persistent schema version and migration entry point for future state upgrades.
Add tests for interrupted writes using temp-file/rename semantics to prove artifacts are never partially committed.
Document where state lives and how upgrades/migrations are handled.

categories.aliases: user interface / usability / display fixes / formatting
categories.day1_tell: Walk the golden path as a first-time user; confirm empty states, long values, and errors all render intentionally.
categories.reasoning: CLI and skill validation docs address user-facing flows, but the evidence does not show explicit empty-state, long-output, or error-rendering polish tests for first-time CLI use.

fix_sites.what: Add examples of empty config, invalid workflow, long values, and actionable error output.
Add golden-output tests for common user-facing failure messages.

categories.aliases: i18n / localization / translations
categories.day1_tell: Feed non-ASCII input end-to-end (CJK, emoji, RTL) and confirm no mangling; locale strings externalized if user-facing.
categories.reasoning: The keyword search found no internationalization/localization evidence, and for this CLI sub-type the relevant missing capability is explicit Unicode/non-ASCII end-to-end handling tests.

fix_sites.what: Add a workflow/task/output test containing CJK text, emoji, and RTL text and assert JSON/CLI output preserves it.
Ensure all persisted and subprocess-exchanged text uses UTF-8 and does not ASCII-escape or corrupt Unicode.

categories.aliases: resource leaks / file handles / memory cleanup / shutdown handling
categories.day1_tell: Run a soak loop and confirm stable handles/memory; SIGTERM mid-work and confirm graceful shutdown.
categories.reasoning: MCP server and contract evidence suggest resource-managed operations, but there is no explicit soak/SIGTERM cleanup proof for handles, processes, or worktrees.

fix_sites.what: Add graceful shutdown handling that closes subprocesses, streams, and temporary resources on SIGTERM.
Add a shutdown test proving in-flight protocol resources are cleaned up deterministically.
Document server lifecycle and cleanup behavior for cancellation and termination.

categories.aliases: SECURITY.md / vulnerability reporting / disclosure policy / security contact
categories.day1_tell: Find the documented vulnerability-reporting channel (SECURITY.md) and confirm a reporter could use it without filing a public issue.
categories.reasoning: SECURITY.md provides a private vulnerability-reporting path and explicitly tells reporters not to open public issues for vulnerabilities or secrets.

categories.aliases: LICENSE / license metadata / copyright / third-party notices
categories.day1_tell: Confirm a LICENSE file exists and the package metadata declares the same license.
categories.reasoning: Release gate and packaging tests check license files and metadata consistency, while NOTICE records provenance obligations.

categories.aliases: CONTRIBUTING / code of conduct / issue templates / PR templates
categories.day1_tell: From CONTRIBUTING.md alone, a new contributor can set up, run tests, and submit a change.
categories.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md, README, setup references, and subagent docs provide contributor setup, deterministic testing expectations, and change/release rules.

categories.aliases: CHANGELOG / keep-a-changelog / dated release notes / breaking-change notes
categories.day1_tell: Open the changelog: latest release has a dated, sectioned entry that calls out breaking changes separately.
categories.reasoning: The changelog follows Keep a Changelog/SemVer and has release links, but the evidence excerpt only shows an Unreleased section and links, not a dated sectioned latest release entry with breaking-change treatment.

fix_sites.what: Add or verify a dated latest-release section with standard subsections and an explicit Breaking Changes subsection when applicable.
Fail release if the current version lacks a dated changelog heading and required section structure.

categories.aliases: lint / linter / static analysis / formatter / type checking in CI
categories.day1_tell: Run the project's lint/typecheck command locally and confirm CI enforces the same check.
categories.reasoning: Static validation, lint/types, and CI enforcement are described in roadmap-like evidence, but the concrete local lint/typecheck command and CI parity are not clearly visible in the cited evidence.

fix_sites.what: Document the exact lint, format, and typecheck commands contributors must run locally.
Ensure the CI pipeline invokes the same lint/typecheck command documented for local use.

categories.aliases: signed releases / checksums / sigstore / SLSA / build provenance
categories.day1_tell: Download a release artifact and verify its checksum or signature by the documented method.
categories.reasoning: The evidence shows SHA-256 digest computation and apparent digest checking in runtime/artifact-related code, which supports some artifact integrity checking. However, it does not demonstrate a documented release-artifact verification method, published checksums, signatures, or provenance for downloadable releases. Therefore it is not fully covered for release integrity/provenance.
categories.pre_escalation_reasoning: Release integrity is optional but applicable, and the evidence shows it is planned rather than documented with downloadable checksums or signatures.

categories.aliases: SBOM / software bill of materials / dependency disclosure
categories.day1_tell: Generate or locate the published SBOM for the latest release.
categories.reasoning: SBOM and supply-chain transparency are optional but applicable to published packages, and the roadmap only lists SBOM generation as future work.

fix_sites.what: Add the command and publication location for the release SBOM.
Generate an SBOM as part of the release gate and include it with artifacts.
Cross-reference the SBOM as the machine-readable dependency/provenance companion to retained notices.

categories.aliases: fuzz testing / property-based tests / fuzzers
categories.day1_tell: Find a fuzz or property-based target exercising the main parser/input boundary; run it briefly.
categories.reasoning: Fuzzing/property-based testing is optional but relevant to workflow/parser boundaries, and the evidence contains only general testing/roadmap references with no fuzz/property target.

fix_sites.what: Add property-style cases or a fuzz harness for workflow/config JSON/TOML parsing boundaries.
Document how to run the parser fuzz/property test briefly during hardening work.

categories.aliases: upgrade guide / UPGRADING.md / deprecation warnings / breaking-change policy
categories.day1_tell: Trigger a deprecated path: it warns with the removal version and a migration pointer; an upgrade guide exists.
categories.reasoning: Deprecation and migration are mentioned conceptually for MCP and setup, but there is no explicit deprecated-path behavior with warning, removal version, and migration pointer.

fix_sites.what: Add a deprecation policy covering warning format, removal version, and migration-guide expectations.
When loading older state/schema paths, emit structured deprecation warnings with removal version and migration instructions.
Reserve a Breaking/Deprecated subsection for every release that introduces a deprecated path.

categories.aliases: privacy policy / data collection disclosure / telemetry opt-out
categories.day1_tell: Find documentation of what data is collected/stored and a working opt-out for any telemetry.
categories.reasoning: Security and roadmap evidence stress private prompts/secrets and local configuration, but there is no dedicated privacy/data-handling disclosure or opt-out statement for telemetry-like data.

fix_sites.what: Add a data-handling section describing what run artifacts, prompts, environment names, and diagnostics are stored locally and what is never collected.
Document any diagnostic/run-artifact retention controls and explicitly state whether the tool phones home or how to opt out if telemetry is added.
